genesis.3.p1.b1.text: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made.

genesis.3.p1.b2.text: Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’

genesis.3.p1.b3.text: We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden, but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, …

genesis.3.p1.b4.text: God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’

genesis.3.p2.b5.text: You will not surely die, … For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.

genesis.3.p2.b6.text: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom,

genesis.3.p2.b7.text: she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.

genesis.3.p3.b8.text: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked;

genesis.3.p3.b9.text: so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.

genesis.3.p3.b10.text: the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day,

genesis.3.p3.b11.text: the man and his wife … hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.

genesis.3.p4.b13.text: I heard Your voice in the garden, … and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.

genesis.3.p5.b14.text: Who told you that you were naked? … Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?

genesis.3.p5.b15.text: The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.

genesis.3.p5.b16.text: What is this you have done?

genesis.3.p5.b17.text: The serpent deceived me, … and I ate.

genesis.3.p6.b18.text: Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life.

genesis.3.p6.b19.text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed.

genesis.3.p6.b20.text: He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.

genesis.3.p7.b21.text: I will sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you will bring forth children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.

genesis.3.p7.b22.text: cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life. Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you,

genesis.3.p7.b23.text: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken.

genesis.3.p7.b24.text: For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.

genesis.3.p8.b25.text: And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.

genesis.3.p8.b26.text: And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.

genesis.3.p9.b27.text: the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...

genesis.3.p9.b28.text: Therefore the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.

genesis.3.p9.b29.text: So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.
